items.summary: Diffusion language models form answers through a sequence of revisable continuous states, but multi-agent systems usually discard those states and make agents communicate only after decoding text. items.summary: Feed-forward 3D Gaussian Splatting (FF3DGS) reconstructs 3D scenes from images in a single forward pass, making it well-suited to applications that must operate within limited resource budgets. items.author: Ziqi Jin, Weiwen Xu, Jiaxi Li, Yujie Zhong et al.

items.summary: Speculative decoding accelerates autoregressive (AR) language models by letting a small model draft tokens serially and a large model verify them in parallel. Starting from a standard AR checkpoint, we fine-tune the large model into a proposer that predicts a block of future tokens in a single forward pass, then use one additional forward pass to verify the proposed block.

items.title: Do You Trust Apple?

items.description: Apple has a lot of trust in terms of delivering integrated products and preserving privacy; the real trust question is if you think Siri AI will justify investing more in their ecosystem.

That wasn’t the remarkable part: what blew the crowd away was when he picked up the just-introduced iBook and walked around while waiting for Disney.com to load.

items.summary: Scene-level 3D generation has long been dominated by 2D multi-view or video diffusion models. items.summary: Scaling laws suggest that increasing model size, training data, and compute generally yields monotonic performance improvements.
